patch.value: Explain moved goal dates between saved resource schedules
Compare saved scheduling inputs with the existing resource scenario engine; prove causes with bounded counterfactual replays and preserve unsupported evidence as gaps.

One estimate change yields exact downstream civil-day delta and causal chain; unchanged rows collapse to references; unsupported inputs remain gaps rather than blamed causes; typed SDK and CLI, bounded TOON/JSON, no-git and public read-only validation.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Overlap rechecked against current CLI declarations and sibling README surfaces: core owns complete reads, status/relationship registries and serialization; pm-graph snapshot-impact compares topology/frontiers but no calendar allocation or computed schedule dates. Reuse resourceScenarios and its strict duration schema; no new scheduler. Saved snapshots are read-only values, no importer/sync, journal, mutation or shared checkpoint. Attribution uses individual counterfactual reversals; interactions without an individually witnessed effect remain gaps. Native statuses resolve through SDK registry roles before engine projection.

value.text: Implemented typed snapshot capture, strict snapshot validation and drift SDK plus gantt snapshot/drift CLI commands. Existing engine supplies all dates. One estimate regression proves exact one-day downstream movement and full prerequisite chain. Public origin/main validation: 117 items, 8 active, 9 relationships, 5 missing estimates, 8 missing owners; explicit hypothetical overrides only. Estimate 60 to 540 minutes moved 8 dates, 3 returned, 3 evaluations, zero gaps, 1160 JSON bytes and 1221 TOON bytes. Read-only non-git archive and deterministic replay preserve durable source hashes. Seeded model now varies all native scheduling fields and random custom SDK role registries; read-only feature introduces no mutations, plans, locks, idempotency keys or shared drainer state.

General rules: every successful replayable producer must fit its consumer transport, and untrusted dictionary names must access own entries only (never Object.prototype values or setters). Fresh fetch shows branch contains origin/main (6 ahead, 0 behind); worktree initially clean. Supplied review and GitHub review comments contain no additional non-blocking findings. value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Both review classes are fixed and adversarial focused tests pass 4/4. The shared schema caps canonical pretty snapshot JSON at 4 MiB; saved-file replay allows 16 MiB including host envelopes/indentation, while controls retain 256 KiB and estimates 64 KiB. All three CLI file paths share a bounded UTF-8 descriptor reader with read-time growth checks and guaranteed close. Calendar/work lookups and schema dispatch use own entries; counterfactual dictionaries reconstruct through Map/Object.fromEntries, preserving prototype-named keys without setters. Existing uncertainty own-entry guards were already correct; fixed status tables and generated brand tokens are trusted closed enums, not user-key dictionaries. No extra non-blocking findings were supplied. Six function-level reversions were caught: old snapshot file cap, missing producer byte cap, missing read-growth check, inherited shared lookup, inherited calendar lookup, and prototype-setter reconstruction. Each failed with ERR_ASSERTION and original source bytes were restored. Tests cover 500 producer transports, 500 prototype-name sequences, complete 2000-item non-git replay and all command reader bounds; packed matrix now exercises those same large envelopes and constructor/__proto__ calendars.
